title: Smile's first test X-ray image shows supernova remnant in Large Magellanic Cloud
excerpt: Smile's first test X-ray image shows supernova remnant in Large Magellanic Cloud
content:
This is one of two first images to be released from the X-ray camera (SXI) on the European-Chinese Smile mission. With SXI, Smile is becoming the first spacecraft to make detailed, long-running X-ray observations of Earth’s magnetic field.

The image shows the remains of a massive star exploding in the Large Magellanic Cloud, around 160 000 light-years away. These million-degree hot ‘supernova remnants’ glow bright in X-ray light, making the Large Magellanic Cloud, and N132D, a great test subject for Smile. Once it begins its real science phase, Smile will actually look at X-rays released at the edge of Earth’s magnetosphere when it is hit by charged particles from the Sun.
